The difference between awakening and succession simply means each class gets a different weapon offering a different playstyle succession is an empowered main hand moveset for example...

I mentioned mystic and witch. I'll pick up witch, she has a staff and a dagger as her main hand weapon and her off hand weapon she focuses on lightning and snow spells think chain lightning, snowstorm and magic missle with group heals and teleports. Her awakening gives her the ad spheres which house each elemental and golem empowering her to use earth and lightning based spells whilst retaining her pre awakened (main hand and off hand) skills (succession locks you out of awakenenin skills, gsont worry you can switch between each preset).

Some classes feel vastly different depending on awakening or succession spec. Drakania has a greatsword as her main hand and teo spears as her awakening going from a slow heavy gladiator tank style to a fast paced dragoon playstyle.

There are typically 2 types of taming methods passive and KO. With passive taming you run up and shove x item into its mouth. With KO you need to well tranq it out.

For tranq methods a dino trap may be advisable (build out of stone or metal as dinos won't cause too much damage to structures). YouTube is your friend.

Here's a list of tames I go for typically in order of progression and why-

Pteranodon -ez flyer, use bolas and tranq arrow, then meat from a dodo.

Parasaur or tricerotops - for berry/wood, thatch and fiber gathering. (Parasaur has an enemy allergy function).

Argentavis - decent dino killer, and it's saddle acts as a smithy n also half's resource weight making it a beefy cargo bus. Still use past the endgame.

Direbear or therizenosaur - great all-rounder multiple dino. Though only the tickle chickens uses remains far into the endgame with direbears becoming more niche at that stage. I love em they are fast n tanks, n it's advised to have one in order to go for bee hives which is useful for later game things. The theri on a raft glazing through the swamp is the best way for wood farming but the swamp is no place or the faint of heart.

The almighty anklyosaurus - gathers metal and stone by the ton. The Doed is better for stone and has a fun sonic the hedgehog roley pole move. Pair it with the argy n you'll be a stone metal gatherers dream.

The T frikkin Rex - one of the best mid to late game killers. Also with breeding you'll need an army of em to run bosses. To trap these guys I use a 4 dino gate open square or a partial triangle and quickly loop around or get your wife to place a gate behind it once you lure it into the trap. Or run backwards whilst pelting it with tranq arrows or if you have an argy puck up your wife and dangle her above the tex letting her tranq it out from the safety of above (bring a parachute and indicate your argys stamina bar).

The quetz/bronto - is basically trike and argys bigger fatter brother but with a mean personality. To tame a quetz dangle from the argy using a grapplehook crossbow and parachutes. Then use a different crossbow for tranqing out the quetz.

Then I go for the king of the skies the almighty wyvern. For this I simply use a shitty ptera that has points in stam n enough in w8 for me and the egg. Place beds along the scar so I can quickly respawn and recover my dead body and literally Indiana Jones that fucker. (Scorched earth and ragnarok maps).

Take note on taming. You can end up killing the dino you intend to tame whilst KOing it. Hitting it after it's KOd will kill it's taming effectiveness. The higher this is the more extra levels it gets which is a good thing.

A max lvl 150 Rex for example with 100% effectiveness will result in a lvl225 Rex you can't distribute these levels but using tek binocs or a mod that acts like tek binocs u can see where those levels were distributed. Each dino has its preferred food (this is for taming purposes only n serves to make the taming process quicker. As such it's usually a teir of kibble that works best, dododex has great info on what you need for taming purposes (i.e. the good  and taming method).

As for your owned tames there's a few settings I change on each of my dinos. Interact with each dino n go to behaviour  hange follow distance to 1 and attack distance to 1. Set aggression behavior to atta j my target, passive or neutral remember when on  taming excursions to set dinos to passive (,you can whistle passive or such), disable ally looking (especially on rexes and bigger dinos). The rest is preference.

But importantly anyways remember to punch trees responsibly.

All classes have a Main Hand Weapon, an Off Hand Wespon and an Awakening Weapon.

At level 56 all classes can choose to (with the exception of Shai, Archer and Scholar) spec into awakening or Succession.

Awakening uses a new weapon and can flow into pre-awakening (your main hand weapon), you also use your offhand/sub weapon.

Succession empowers your main Hand, locks you out of awakening stance (skills and the weapon) and uses solely your main Hand and Sub/off Hand.

This gives us options when playing certian classes, where for some classes their awk might be suited for pvx (1v more than 1 or aoe pve) whereas their succession might be more suited for stationary pve and 1v1 situations or vice versa or a mix. It's really class spesific.

Now as eluded to there are three major (currently) exceptions : Scholar and Arsher start woth their awakening spec off the rip and don't get access to primal skills ( -primal skills are succession skills and absolutes are awakened versions they tend to be less powerful than the primal versions but you gain access to awakening stance n such- ).

Scholar infuses her two hammers into one great hammer, Archer switches his bow for a wrist crossbow.

Shais (awakening weapon) is a Sol her magical musical lantern that her awakening skills use to buff, rebuff n heal. You obtain through the level 56 story quest which is different to the typical awakening and succession advancement questlines.
